protocols.name: Severe / life-threatening bleeding
exemplars: he cut his leg and blood is everywhere
bleeding will not stop help
she got stabbed in the arm
blood is spurting out of the wound
deep cut bleeding heavily
gunshot wound to the leg
his hand is gushing blood
blood is pumping out of the cut
he slashed his arm on glass huge amounts of blood
when should i use a tourniquet

pressure.text: Press hard on the wound right now with a clean cloth, towel, or your hands — hard, direct pressure is what stops bleeding. If you have gloves or a plastic bag, put them on your hands first.
donot: Do not remove any object stuck in the wound — press around it instead.

lie_down.text: Have them lie down. Keep pressing hard without letting go. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top — never remove the soaked layer.

q_stopping.prompt: After 10 minutes of firm pressure, is the bleeding slowing down?

bandage.text: Keep the pressure on. If you have a bandage, wrap it firmly over the padding to hold the pressure — snug, but fingers or toes should stay pink and warm.

q_limb.prompt: Is the wound on an arm or a leg?

tourniquet.text: If you have a tourniquet, put it 5 to 8 centimeters above the wound — not on a joint — and tighten until the bleeding stops. No tourniquet? Use a folded scarf or tie with a stick to twist it tight. Write down or remember the exact time you applied it.
donot: Do not loosen or remove a tourniquet once applied.
Do not cover the tourniquet — responders must see it.

pack_wound.text: Pack the wound: push clean cloth or gauze directly into it, filling the space, and keep pressing hard on top with both hands. Do not let go.

shock_watch.text: Keep them lying down and warm — cover them with a coat or blanket. Reassure them and keep talking.
donot: Do not give them anything to eat or drink.
Do not raise the wounded limb instead of pressing — pressure comes first.

monitor_bleed.text: Keep pressure on until help arrives. Tell me immediately if they become pale, cold, confused or drowsy — and never let go of the pressure.

protocols.name: Cuts, scrapes and small wounds
exemplars: i cut my finger chopping vegetables
my kid scraped his knee
small cut how do i clean it
i have a scratch that is bleeding a little
grazed my elbow falling off the bike
paper cut bleeding

q_severe_check.prompt: Quick check: is it bleeding heavily, spurting, gaping open, or very deep?

wash_hands.text: Wash your own hands first if you can. Press gently on the wound with a clean cloth until any bleeding stops — usually a few minutes.

clean_wound.text: Rinse the wound under clean running water for a few minutes. Wash around it with mild soap. Gently remove loose dirt with a clean, damp gauze.
donot: Do not pour hydrogen peroxide, iodine or alcohol into the wound — they damage the tissue.
Do not scrub hard.

dress_wound.text: Pat it dry, apply a thin layer of antibiotic ointment or petroleum jelly if available, and cover with a plaster or sterile dressing. Change it daily and keep it clean and dry.

q_tetanus.prompt: Was the cut from something dirty or rusty, or is their tetanus shot more than 5 years old or unknown?

tetanus_advice.text: See a doctor or pharmacist within 48 hours about a tetanus booster — dirty or rusty wounds carry tetanus risk.

monitor_wound.text: See a doctor if it gapes open and might need closing, would not stop bleeding, or over the next days becomes more red, swollen, warm, oozing, or a fever starts — those are infection signs.

protocols.name: Nosebleed
exemplars: my nose is bleeding a lot
how do i stop a nosebleed
kid has a bloody nose
nosebleed will not stop
blood pouring from my nose

sit_forward.text: Sit them down and lean them FORWARD — head tilted slightly down, so blood does not run down the throat.
donot: Do not tilt the head back.
Do not lie them down.

pinch.text: Pinch the soft part of the nose, just below the bony bridge, firmly closed. Hold for 10 to 15 minutes without peeking. Breathe through the mouth. Spit out any blood in the mouth.

q_stopped_nb.prompt: After 10 to 15 minutes of steady pinching, has the bleeding stopped?

pinch_again.text: Pinch again, a little lower and firmer, for another 15 minutes. A cold pack on the bridge of the nose can help.

ems_nb.text: Bleeding beyond 30 minutes of good pressure needs urgent medical care — go to an emergency department, or call emergency services if it is very heavy, they feel faint, or they take blood thinners.

aftercare_nb.text: For the next day: no nose blowing, no picking, no heavy lifting, and sneeze with the mouth open. A thin smear of petroleum jelly inside the nostril keeps it from cracking again.

monitor_nb.text: If it restarts, do the same: lean forward and pinch for 15 minutes. Frequent nosebleeds are worth mentioning to a doctor.

protocols.name: Amputation (severed body part)
exemplars: he cut his finger off with the saw
her hand got severed in the machine
the lawnmower cut off his toes
amputated finger what do i do with it
his thumb was chopped off

control_bleed_amp.text: Stop the bleeding first: press hard on the stump with clean cloth. If bleeding from an arm or leg will not stop with pressure, apply a tourniquet 5 to 8 centimeters above the wound and note the time.

dress_stump.text: Cover the stump with a moist sterile dressing or clean cloth and bandage firmly. Lay them down, keep them warm, and reassure them.
donot: Do not give them anything to eat or drink.

preserve_part.text: Now the severed part: wrap it in clean, slightly damp gauze or cloth. Put it in a sealed plastic bag. Put that bag on top of ice or ice water in another container.
donot: Do not put the part directly on ice.
Do not submerge the part in water.
Do not wash or scrub the part.

label_part.text: Keep the part with the person — hand it to the paramedics. Reattachment works best within hours, so make sure it travels with them.

monitor_amp.text: Keep firm pressure on the stump and keep them warm and lying down. Tell me if they become pale, sweaty, confused or drowsy.

protocols.name: Object embedded in a wound
exemplars: a piece of glass is stuck in her arm
he fell on a spike and it is still in his leg
knife is still in the wound do i pull it out
nail went through his foot
metal rod impaled his thigh

leave_it.text: Leave the object exactly where it is — it is plugging the wound and pulling it out can cause massive bleeding.
donot: Do not pull the object out.
Do not press directly on the object.

pad_around.text: Press on the wound edges around the object, then build padding around it — rolled bandages or cloth on each side — until the padding is as high as the object, and bandage over the padding without pressing the object.

q_big_object.prompt: Is it a large object, in the chest, belly, neck or eye, or is there heavy bleeding?

ems_embedded.text: Call emergency services now. Keep them as still as possible and keep the object stabilized.

urgent_care_embedded.text: Even small embedded objects need a professional to remove them safely — go to urgent care or an emergency department now, keeping the object padded and still.

monitor_embedded.text: Keep the object still and the person calm. Tell me if bleeding increases or they feel faint, pale or sweaty.

protocols.name: Head injury / concussion
exemplars: my son fell and hit his head hard
she banged her head on the cupboard
hit his head playing football possible concussion
toddler fell off the couch onto his head
i hit my head and feel dizzy
baby fell off the couch big bump on his head

q_red_flags_head.prompt: Check these now: were they knocked out even briefly, have they vomited, are they confused or slurring, is one pupil bigger, are they having a seizure, or is there fluid or blood from an ear or the nose?

ems_head.text: Call emergency services now — those are danger signs after a head injury. Keep them still and lying down with head and shoulders slightly raised. If they vomit, roll them to their side keeping head and neck in line.
donot: Do not give them painkillers, food or drink.
Do not let them go to sleep unattended before help arrives.

monitor_head_sev.text: Keep them still and watch closely. Tell me immediately if they become drowsy, vomit again, or stop responding.

q_conscious_head.prompt: Are they fully awake, talking normally, and acting like themselves?

cold_pack_head.text: Have them stop all activity and rest sitting or lying down. Hold a cold pack wrapped in cloth on the bump for up to 20 minutes.

watch_24.text: Someone should watch them closely for the next 24 hours, and it is fine for them to sleep — just check on them regularly. No sport, screens minimal, no alcohol.

monitor_head.text: Go straight to emergency care if any of these appear: repeated vomiting, worsening headache, unusual drowsiness or confusion, seizure, weakness or numbness, or clear fluid from the nose or ears. See a doctor before returning to sport.

protocols.name: Suspected spinal (neck / back) injury
exemplars: he fell off the roof and his neck hurts
diving accident he cannot feel his legs
car crash she says her back hurts badly
possible spinal injury after falling from a ladder
he cannot move his legs after the fall

keep_still.text: Tell them not to move at all. Keep them exactly in the position you found them.
donot: Do not move them unless they are in immediate danger like fire or traffic.
Do not remove a helmet unless you must open the airway.
Do not put anything under their head.

hold_head.text: Kneel behind their head. Hold it steady with a hand on each side, keeping head, neck and back in one line. Stay like this until paramedics take over.

q_responsive_sp.prompt: Are they awake and breathing normally?

to_cpr_sp.text: Breathing comes before the spine — we start CPR now, keeping the head as steady as you can.

reassure_sp.text: Keep them warm with a blanket laid over them and keep talking calmly. If they vomit, roll them to their side as one unit — ideally with helpers — keeping head, neck and back aligned.

monitor_sp.text: Hold their head steady and keep them still until help arrives. Tell me if their breathing changes or they stop responding.

protocols.name: Broken bone (fracture)
exemplars: i think he broke his arm
her leg looks broken after the fall
bone is sticking out of his leg
broken wrist from falling off a bike
my ankle snapped i heard a crack
kid fell off the trampoline arm looks bent

q_open_or_major.prompt: Is the bone poking through the skin, is the leg, hip or thigh involved, is the limb bent at a wrong angle, or are they pale, cold or faint?

ems_fracture.text: Call emergency services now. Keep them still and support the limb exactly where it lies. If bone is exposed, cover the wound lightly with a clean dressing and press around it — not on the bone — to control bleeding.
donot: Do not push the bone back in.
Do not straighten the limb.
Do not let them eat or drink — surgery may be needed.

monitor_fracture_sev.text: Keep the limb supported and them warm and still until help arrives. Tell me if they become pale, sweaty or drowsy, or the limb goes numb or blue.

immobilize.text: Keep the injured part completely still, supported in the position found. For an arm, support it against the body with a cushion, folded towel or a sling. Remove rings or watches near the injury now, before swelling.
donot: Do not straighten or force the limb.
Do not test it by making them move or walk on it.

ice_fracture.text: Put a cold pack wrapped in cloth over the area for up to 20 minutes to ease pain and swelling.

transport_fracture.text: They need an X-ray: go to urgent care or the emergency department now, keeping the limb supported and still. Call emergency services instead if you cannot move them without pain, or the limb is numb, blue or cold.

monitor_fracture.text: Keep the limb still and elevated if possible. Tell me if fingers or toes beyond the injury turn numb, blue or cold — that is urgent.

protocols.name: Sprain or strain
exemplars: i twisted my ankle running
sprained wrist from falling
rolled my ankle it is swelling
pulled a muscle in my back lifting
my knee twisted and now it hurts to walk

q_fracture_doubt.prompt: Can they put any weight on it or use it at all, and does it look a normal shape?

to_fracture.text: Cannot bear weight or looks deformed — treat it as a possible break.

rice_rest.text: Rest it: stop the activity and take the weight off the joint.

rice_ice.text: Ice it: cold pack or ice wrapped in a cloth, 15 to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours for the first day or two.
donot: Do not put ice directly on the skin.
Do not apply heat, alcohol rubs or massage in the first 2 days.

rice_compress.text: Compress it: wrap with an elastic bandage, snug but not tight — toes or fingers must stay pink and warm. Loosen it if it throbs.

rice_elevate.text: Elevate it above heart level whenever sitting or lying, especially the first 48 hours.

monitor_sprain.text: See a doctor if they cannot bear weight after a day or two, the pain or swelling is severe or not improving, or anything feels numb. Gentle movement can restart as pain allows.

protocols.name: Dislocated joint
exemplars: his shoulder popped out of the socket
dislocated my finger playing basketball
her kneecap popped out
shoulder dislocated again what do i do
elbow looks out of joint

no_reduce.text: Do not try to pop the joint back in — that can tear vessels and nerves. Keep it exactly where it is.
donot: Do not pull, twist or force the joint back into place.
Do not let them eat or drink — sedation may be needed to fix it.

support_dislocation.text: Support the joint in the most comfortable position with a sling, cushion or rolled clothing. A wrapped cold pack over it eases pain, up to 20 minutes.

q_circulation_d.prompt: Below the joint — are fingers or toes pink, warm, and can they feel your touch?

ems_d.text: Call emergency services now — numb, blue or cold beyond the joint means blood flow or nerves are compromised.

transport_d.text: Get them to an emergency department now with the joint supported — dislocations need prompt professional reduction.

monitor_d.text: Keep it supported and still. Tell me if the hand or foot beyond it becomes numb, blue or cold.

protocols.name: Crush injury / trapped under weight
exemplars: his leg is crushed under the car
she is pinned under a fallen wall
hand caught in the machine
he got run over and his leg is trapped
heavy shelf fell and crushed her foot

q_can_release.prompt: Has the person been trapped for LESS than 15 minutes, and can you remove the weight safely without danger to you?

release_now.text: Remove the weight now if it is safe, then control any bleeding with firm direct pressure and cover wounds with clean cloth.

after_release.text: Keep them still and warm, and treat what you find: pressure for bleeding, support for possible broken bones. Assume a spinal injury if the crush was to the body — keep them still.

do_not_release.text: If they have been trapped more than 15 minutes, or you cannot lift it safely, leave the weight in place — releasing a long crush without medical care can cause deadly toxin release. Comfort them, keep them warm, and wait for rescuers.
donot: Do not lift a weight that has crushed a limb for over 15 minutes.
Do not use a makeshift tourniquet on a crushed limb unless it is bleeding heavily.

monitor_crush.text: Stay with them, keep them warm, and keep talking to them. Tell me immediately if they stop responding or their breathing changes.

protocols.name: Open chest wound
exemplars: he was stabbed in the chest
gunshot to the chest he is breathing strangely
there is a hole in her chest and it makes bubbling sounds
open chest wound what do i do
chest stab wound air is coming out of it

position_chest.text: Help them into the position where breathing feels easiest — usually sitting up or leaning toward the injured side. If an object is still in the chest, leave it in place.

expose_seal.text: Leave the wound open to the air — do not seal it airtight and do not pile dressings over it. If blood is flowing, press around the wound edges with a clean cloth, letting air still escape.
donot: Do not tape plastic or airtight dressings over the wound.
Do not remove an embedded object.

monitor_chest.text: Stay with them and keep them as still and calm as possible. Tell me immediately if breathing gets worse or they stop responding — if they become unresponsive we will start CPR.

protocols.name: Open abdominal wound
exemplars: he was stabbed in the stomach
deep cut on the belly and something is bulging out
her intestines are showing from the wound
open wound on the abdomen bleeding a lot

position_abd.text: Lay them on their back with knees bent up, supported by a rolled coat or pillow under the knees — this relaxes the belly.

cover_abd.text: If organs are visible, do not touch or push them back. Cover them with a moist, clean dressing or cloth, then loosely with plastic wrap or foil to keep them from drying. Otherwise, press firmly around the wound with clean cloth to slow bleeding.
donot: Do not push organs back inside.
Do not press directly on exposed organs.
Do not give anything to eat or drink.

monitor_abd.text: Keep them warm, still and reassured. Tell me if they become pale, cold, confused or unresponsive.

protocols.name: Knocked-out tooth
sources: International Association of Dental Traumatology guidelines
exemplars: his tooth got knocked out playing hockey
my tooth came out whole after a fall
kid knocked out a front tooth
tooth knocked out do i put it in milk
adult tooth fell out from a punch

q_adult_tooth.prompt: Is it an adult (permanent) tooth — not a baby tooth?

baby_tooth.text: Do not put a baby tooth back in — it can damage the adult tooth underneath. Have the child bite gently on a clean gauze pad to stop bleeding and see a dentist today.

handle_crown.text: Pick the tooth up by the crown — the white chewing part. Never touch the root. If dirty, rinse it briefly, a few seconds, in milk or saline; do not scrub or dry it.
donot: Do not scrub or wipe the root.
Do not let the tooth dry out.

reinsert.text: Best option: push it gently back into its socket right away, facing the right way, and have them bite softly on a cloth to hold it. If you cannot, store it in cold milk, saline, or inside their cheek if they are old enough not to swallow it.
donot: Do not store the tooth in plain water.

dentist_now.text: Get to a dentist or emergency department immediately — the tooth survives best if replanted within 30 to 60 minutes.

monitor_tooth.text: Bite on gauze for bleeding gums. If there was a hard head knock too, watch for headache, vomiting or confusion — those need emergency care.

protocols.name: Blister
exemplars: i have a big blister on my heel
should i pop this blister
blister from new shoes what do i do
my blister burst is that bad

leave_blister.text: Leave it unpopped if you can — the skin over it is the best protection against infection. Wash gently, pat dry, and cover with a cushioned plaster or blister pad.
donot: Do not deliberately pop a blister.
Do not peel off the skin over a burst blister.

burst_care.text: Let the fluid drain, wash with mild soap and water, keep the loose skin as a natural dressing, apply petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment, and cover with a clean non-stick dressing. Change daily.

monitor_blister.text: See a doctor if it becomes more red, warm, swollen, oozes pus, or if you have diabetes or poor circulation — foot wounds then need professional care.

protocols.name: Splinter
exemplars: i have a splinter in my finger
how do i get a splinter out
kid has a thorn stuck in her hand
glass sliver in my foot

q_deep_splinter.prompt: Is it small and near the surface — you can see its end?

deep_splinter.text: Deep, large, or fully buried splinters — especially glass, metal, or under a nail or near the eye — should be removed by a professional. Cover it lightly and see a doctor or urgent care.
donot: Do not dig deeply into the skin with a needle.

remove_splinter.text: Wash the area and your hands with soap and water. Grip the splinter end with clean tweezers close to the skin and pull it out at the same angle it went in, slowly and steadily.

after_splinter.text: Squeeze gently to let a drop of blood flush the track, wash again, and cover with a plaster. Check tetanus status if it was dirty wood.

monitor_splinter.text: Watch for infection over the next days: growing redness, warmth, swelling or pus means see a doctor.

protocols.name: Bruise
exemplars: huge bruise forming on my shin
bumped my thigh and it is turning purple
how do i treat a bad bruise
kid has a black eye from a ball

cold_bruise.text: Put a cold pack or ice wrapped in a cloth on it for 15 to 20 minutes, several times over the first day. Elevate the area if you can.
donot: Do not put ice directly on bare skin.

monitor_bruise.text: It should fade over 1 to 2 weeks. See a doctor if the swelling is severe, they take blood thinners, the bruise appeared with no injury, or pain makes the limb unusable — and for a black eye with any change in vision, get emergency care.
